subject: Inbound attachments: PHI handling and eligibility for hosted vs. private
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@lakeshorehealth.com>

Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@lakeshorehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify: inbound attachments that may contain PHI (eligibility)

Hi Jasmine,

Quick intro — I'm Samir on Lakeshore's integrations team. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will ingest clinician notes and occasional patient-submitted documents (PDFs, images). Before we spin up anything, legal/security asked two quick questions:

1) If our users upload attachments that include PHI, does Redwood's hosted API path allow us to keep that data in the hosted environment, or do we need Dedicated/Private to be HIPAA-eligible?
2) Is there an inbound-attachments policy we can reference (accepted file types, max size, virus scanning, retention) and an example routing diagram for how attachments are proxied/stored?

We'd like to decide whether to pursue a Dedicated reservation or keep this on your hosted offering for the MVP. If this ends up needing a BAA and Dedicated deployment, we need to know that early.

Thanks — can you point us to any docs or a short note on the eligibility boundary?

Best,
Samir
Samir Rao
Integrations Manager, Lakeshore Health
samir@lakeshorehealth.com

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front: hosted API can be used for non-PHI and low-risk metadata, but for any attachments that contain PHI we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment paired with an executed BAA.

A few clarifying bullets so we can give a specific recommendation:
- Do the attachments need to be sent as raw files to the model (i.e., content to be parsed by an LLM) or are they only stored and referenced (OCR/processing happens on your side)?
- Typical sizes and throughput (avg file size, expected daily uploads).
- Are you able to pre-redact (PII/PHI) before sending, or will Lakeshore rely on our extraction pipeline?

I've attached a quick routing matrix showing the two recommended flows (hosted non-PHI path vs. dedicated PHI path) and the controls we apply. See attachment: PHI_Routing_Matrix.xlsx (stub).

I'll loop in our infra lead to describe presigned/workflow options and to confirm retention and scanning defaults.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Security & Compliance PM
Redwood Inference

Hi all — adding technical detail from engineering:

- Hosted offering: we do not recommend routing raw PHI attachments through the hosted multi-tenant inference path. Hosted will persist short-term logs/telemetry and has transient caches that are not covered under our standard BAA posture.
- Dedicated/Private: supports customer-controlled storage for attachments (S3 in customer project or VPC-mounted storage). When on Dedicated + BAA, attachments can be configured to never be written to shared clusters, and we provide options: presigned-upload (customer directly to S3), server-side-scan (virus + PII detection), or on-the-fly streaming to model with KV cache purging.
- Default file handling controls: max upload 25MB (configurable for Dedicated), automatic MIME-type validation, optional antivirus scan step, and configurable retention TTL.

I've attached a small diagram of the presigned flow we recommend for Dedicated (s3_presigned_flow.png). If Lakeshore wants to keep uploads on your side and only send metadata or pre-extracted text to Redwood, that's the simplest route and keeps you in hosted without PHI touches.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood
Attachment: s3_presigned_flow.png (stub)

Hi — thanks, understood. Action items and proposed deliverables below: 

1) BAA: We can sign Lakeshore's BAA or provide our BAA draft. I'll attach our standard BAA draft and start the DocuSign exchange. (Link: https://app.docusign.com/documents/XYZ-BAA-Draft)
2) SOC 2: I'll share our latest SOC 2 Type II report via a secure drive link (will grant view-only).
3) Retention controls: see attached short doc: redwood-allowed-data-types.md which lists default TTLs and config knobs; short summary: hosted transient telemetry retained 7 days by default, Dedicated attachments TTL configurable (default 30 days), permanent archival only with explicit config.
4) Malware scanning: For Dedicated we offer an optional server-side AV scan; we can enable it as part of onboarding. Hosted does not run AV on customer uploads.
5) DPIA guidance: We'll include a short DPIA note outlining responsibilities; Redwood treats customer-provided PHI as in-scope for customer DPIA and provides evidence templates.

Provisioning lead time for a standard Dedicated pool is ~3–4 weeks after contract and 1 week for security onboarding; expedited options exist for enterprise contracts.

Next steps: I'll upload the SOC 2 and BAA draft to the drive link above and send a separate DocuSign invite. Dev, can you confirm the default max upload and whether we can set the default TTL to 14 days for Lakeshore during onboarding?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Security & Compliance PM, Redwood
